entries.sanskrit:
ततः सप्तदशे जन्म तयोर् लोक-भयङ्-करम् ।

हिरण्याक्ष-प्रभावश् च वर्ण्यते दिग्-जयेऽद्भुतः ॥

क्षेमं विधास्यति \[३.१६.३७\] इति ब्रह्म-वचनानन्तरं । शङ्कया त्यक्ताः ॥१॥
pairs: the birth of those two, causing fear to the worlds
wondrous in the conquest of the directions
entries.literal_english: Thereafter, in the seventeenth chapter, the birth of the two sons—terrifying to the worlds—and the wondrous prowess of Hiraṇyākṣa in his conquest of the directions are described. After Brahmā’s statement, “He will bring about welfare” (3.16.37), they were freed from apprehension.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

entries.sanskrit: भर्तुर् आदेशात् \"लोकान् क्रन्दयिष्यति\" इति तद्-वाक्यात् अपत्याभ्यां सर्व-लोकोपद्रवम् अपत्यं प्रति विष्णु-हस्ततो वधाद् वा शङ्कमाना ॥२॥
pairs: the three worlds together with their protectors
they will repeatedly make cry out
entries.literal_english: Because of her husband’s prediction—“O fierce one, they will repeatedly make the three worlds and their protectors cry out” (3.14.39)—she was apprehensive about her two offspring, fearing that they would bring trouble upon the gods.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

entries.literal_english: “There” means at that time. “Occurred” means arose. They carried great fear on every side.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

pairs: regions of the earth together with the mountains
rose; this is to be supplied
entries.literal_english: “The earth together with the mountains” means the regions of the earth along with the mountains. With “comets,” the sense “rose” is to be supplied.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

pairs: the imitation of the sound of a violent wind
entries.literal_english: “Phūt-kāra” imitates the sound of a violent wind. “Lords of trees” means great trees. Whirlwinds themselves were its army, and dust itself was its banner.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

pairs: the host of lights, such as the sun, was obscured
entries.literal_english: The lightnings were as if laughing loudly. By the mass of clouds, the host of lights such as the sun was obscured. “A place” means any location; it was not seen even slightly.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

pairs: the sea-creatures within it were agitated
with reservoirs, wells, and the like
entries.literal_english: “Vārdhi” is the ocean, as if distressed in mind. Its waves had risen, and the creatures such as makaras dwelling within it were agitated. “With reservoirs” means together with tanks, wells, and the like; their lotuses were dried up.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

pairs: of the sun and moon when seized by Rāhu
sounds like the rumbling of chariots
entries.literal_english: “Paridhayaḥ” means halos. “Together with Rāhu” means the sun and moon when seized by Rāhu. “Nirghātāḥ” are thunderclaps without clouds; sounds like the rumbling of chariots arose from mountain caves.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

entries.literal_english: The cries were those of jackals and owls together. “Śivāḥ” means the female jackals.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

entries.literal_english: “Village-lions” means dogs.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

pairs: the characteristic sound of an ass
entries.literal_english: “Harsh” means sharp. O Kṣattṛ! “Khārkāra” is the characteristic sound of asses; “rabhasa” is the agitation caused by it. “Varūthaśaḥ” means in groups.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

pairs: from the sound of the asses
entries.literal_english: They were frightened by the sound of the asses and cried out on every side.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

entries.literal_english: The cows became frightened and yielded blood. “The divine images wept” means that tears flowed from the images.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

entries.literal_english: “The most auspicious” refers to Jupiter, Mercury, and the like, together with the many stars. The other cruel planets, such as Mars, overtook them, moved in retrograde courses, and came into conflict.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

entries.sanskrit: दृष्ट्वेति । ब्रह्म-पुत्रान् सनकादीन् ऋते ब्रह्म-सृष्टाः । सर्वा एव प्रजा अतत्-तत्त्व-विदो भीता विश्व-सम्प्लवं मेनिरे । देवास् तु ब्रह्म-वाक्यात् तत्त्व-विदोऽभीता आसन्, न तु विश्व-सम्प्लवं मेनिरे इत्य् अर्थः ॥१५॥
pairs: because they knew of their own curse and the rest
entries.literal_english: “Except the sons of Brahmā” means apart from them, because they knew of their own curse and the circumstances connected with it.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

entries.sanskrit: ताव् इति । अत्रानयोर् अणिमादि-शक्त्या गूढ-स्थितौ टीका-सम्मतिश् च ॥१६॥
entries.literal_english: “Their own prowess becoming manifest” means that the prowess already established in them beforehand was now becoming evident.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

entries.literal_english: “The quarters were blocked” means the directions were filled by them. Their armlets flashed upon their arms. The form “aṅgadā” is an archaic feminine usage. A beautiful girdle adorned the waist.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

pairs: was born first from her body
the one whom Diti delivered first
by reversal of the order of entry
the order of birth from the mother
entries.literal_english: Of the twins, the one whose seed had entered first was Hiraṇyakaśipu, while the one whom Diti physically delivered first was Hiraṇyākṣa. The point is that when the seed entering the womb divides into two in sequence, twins result, but their birth from the mother takes place in the reverse order of entry. Thus the one conceived first is born second, and the one conceived second is born first.

pairs: puffed up by the strength of his arms
entries.literal_english: He was puffed up by the strength of his arms and, because of Brahmā’s boon, feared death from no quarter.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

entries.literal_english: “Raṇam” means battle.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

pairs: a great mace resting on his shoulder
entries.literal_english: His speed was irresistible; his golden anklets rang, and a great mace rested on his shoulder. “By mind” means by valor, “by prowess” means by strength, and “by the boon” means by the boon he had received. Thus he was puffed up and unrestrained. “Nililyire” means that the gods hid themselves.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

entries.literal_english: “By his own splendor” means by his radiance. Seeing—understanding—that they had vanished, he did not find the intoxicated gods. On the variant reading “klībān,” the sense is “devoid of manliness.”
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

entries.literal_english: No commentary.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

entries.literal_english: “Sanna” means dejected or sunk; their minds were so. By his splendor they were overpowered and overwhelmed.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

pairs: with the iron or mūrvā-bound mace
mūrvā is the name of a kind of grass
entries.literal_english: He struck the great waves. “Maurvyā” may mean with an iron implement, or with a weapon firmly bound by a cord made from the grass called mūrvā. He reached the city named Vibhāvarī.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

entries.sanskrit: असुर-लोकस्य पातालस्य पालकम् । प्रलब्धुम् उपहसितुं प्रणिपत्य ॥२७॥
entries.literal_english: “The world of the asuras” means Pātāla, and he was its protector. “Pralabdhum” means to mock; for that purpose Hiraṇyākṣa bowed down.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

entries.literal_english: “Yat” has the sense “because”: because formerly you performed the Rājasūya sacrifice.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

pairs: retirement from the sport of battle and the like
entries.literal_english: “Upaśama” means retirement from the sport of battle and similar pursuits.
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

entries.sanskrit: युद्ध-मार्ग-निपुणं त्वां यस् तोषयिष्यति तम् इहि गच्छ । गृणते स्तुवन्ति ॥३०॥
pairs: skilled in the ways of battle
entries.literal_english: Go to that one who will satisfy you, who are skilled in the ways of battle. “Gṛṇate” means “they praise.”
entries.source_note: Directly keyed to the pinned vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam Śrīdhara Svāmī block.

entries.literal_english: “Ārāt” means soon. “Vismaya” here means one whose pride has disappeared. “Vīra-śaya” is the battlefield. “Forms” means incarnations such as Varāha.
